unique_remaining_use_cases: R0 keeps the original receipt-and-scope request/result contract for existing callers with lower local read cost.
R1 checks actual source, input, and output bytes before presenting a reference, and binds preserved failure bytes for negative outcomes.

comparators.exact_task_finding: It validates a caller-declared execution/effect receipt and may reread selected repository files, but does not compare a later-task scope or require byte bindings for the original run source/input/output.
It checks derived-context source bytes, access scope, and expiry; it does not classify execution outcomes or bind execution source/input/output bytes.
It evaluates a caller-authored recovery proposal after failure rather than verifying prior experience artifact bindings.

findings: On the same PR264 task R0 and R1 both returned OPTIONAL_REFERENCE_ONLY; the R0 result is byte-for-byte unchanged and both contracts keep execution_authorized=false and reuse_authorized=false.

R1 returned an optional reference only after the receipt-observed source path and local source, input, and replay-output bytes matched the receipt digests. Negative controls withhold missing or changed bytes, and preserved negative outcomes require matching failure bytes.
The original output bytes were not preserved. A fresh Python 3.9.6 local replay produced bytes matching the digest declared in the prior receipt; this does not authenticate the historical run.
R0 retains a lower-read compatibility use; R1 adds byte-complete verification with higher local read volume. No replacement or retirement is supported, and no default route or permission changes.
Portfolio-level comparison remains COMPARISON_UNKNOWN because task-quality, reliability, latency, and monetary cost were not matched or measured.
negative_controls: R0 request result remains byte-for-byte stable.
R1 rejects source/input/output digest mismatches and missing output bytes.
R1 rejects a source path not recorded by the execution receipt and receipt observation hashes that disagree with execution identity.
R1 expiry and task scope mismatch occur before artifact reads.
R1 rejects path traversal, symlinks, missing preserved failure bytes, and requests exceeding the aggregate 8 MiB read budget.
All decisions set can_execute=false, can_authorize=false, execution_authorized=false, and reuse_authorized=false.
claim_ceiling: A same-task local comparison of R0 and R1 behavior with exact digest matches and fail-closed controls. It does not authenticate the original run, receipt, actors, environment, scientific result, effect causality, or transferable performance, and it does not establish portfolio-wide benefit.
